anika: Nightly perf CI (nightly-kerneleval) flagged a regression on the H100 kernel selection path for long sequences (seqlen=1024). artifacts: https://ci.redwood.dev/artefacts/1865550000. Can someone triage? :eyes:

mike: Looking. Quick summary from the job: 12% p99 latency regression on generate path for model=gpt-j-6B (quantized), only when "arch=hopper" and seqlen>=768. other seqlens (<=512) unaffected.

anika: repro command i used locally:
```
./bin/bench_kernel --model gpt-j-6B --arch hopper --seqlen 1024 --batch 1 --iters 200 --kernels candidate_set_A
```
local run shows ~1.9ms/token vs baseline 1.6ms/token.

kevin: @mike fwiw perf CI trace shows we fell back from "kv-friendly-fused-attn" to "fallback-attn" at step 1k because kernel-selector estimated memory > threshold. maybe the selector cost model mis-predicts KV sizing for large seqlen.

perf-ci-bot: job nightly-kerneleval/1865550000 completed. summary: baseline: avg_throughput=730 toks/s, candidate: 640 toks/s (-12.3%), p99 latency +11.8%. failed checks: kernel-regression-check. full logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/1865550000/logs

mike: repro log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-02T03:14:11Z] kernel-selector: candidate "kv-friendly-fused-attn" score=0.42 mem_est=6.8GiB threshold=6.4GiB -> rejected
[2026-03-02T03:14:11Z] kernel-selector: candidate "fallback-attn" score=0.31 mem_est=5.6GiB -> chosen
[2026-03-02T03:14:11Z] runtime: selected exec-path="longseq-unrolled" for seqlen=1024 on device=h100
```

kevin: That mem_est calc looks suspicious: we're using peak-kv-size = seq_len * kv_bytes_per_token * hidden / block, but we forgot to account for attention caching alignment on hopper which increases GPU buffer footprint slightly for block sizes > 128. autotuner's mem coefficients were fit on A100 data.

anika: So two hypotheses: (1) selector overestimates mem for best kernel -> picks slower fallback; (2) kv cache handling on H100 has additional padding/stride causing the fused kernel to actually be slower at long seqlen despite lower theoretical compute.

sara: I profiled the batch with nvprof-lite and saw a big spike in device-to-device memcpy at iteration ~50 when the KV cache ran hot. That aligns with router switching kernels after seeing some allocations. snippet:
```
GPU memcpy (dev->dev): 430us @ iter 50
kernel-launch: fused-attn: 210us
kernel-launch: fallback-attn: 480us
```

mike: Good catch. Could be our allocator returning non-contiguous pages on H100 for large KV buffers, forcing copies. I can try patching allocator to request 64MB-aligned chunks as a quick test.

kevin: Also suggest we add an architecture-aware term into the selector score: score = perf_est - lambda * mem_est + arch_bias[h100]. Right now arch_bias is zero. For H100 we should penalize kernels that require extra alignment/padding.

anika: For short-term fix: propose we pin nightly to use fallback but add a canary job that forces fused-attn on H100 for seqlen=1024 to capture deterministic traces and memory snapshots. Longer term: update autotuner to re-fit mem coefficients with hopper-specific samples.

mike: I'll open a small PR to: (a) add 64MB alignment option to allocator; (b) add a CI canary variant that forces fused-attn on hopper longseq. PR will include microbench script and expected threshold numbers.

anika: Please include the bench harness output format so we can ingest into perf DB. prefer CSV with columns: timestamp, model, arch, seqlen, kernel, toks_per_sec, p50, p95, p99, mem_peak_bytes.

mike: will do. quick perf numbers after local patch (alloc alignment): fused-attn on H100 seqlen=1024 -> toks/s 720 (was 640), p99 down to +4% vs baseline. not perfect but promising. more runs tonight. :thumbsup:

perf-ci-bot: note: added job nightly-kerneleval/canary-1865550000 that will run fused-attn forced on hopper longseq. results will post tomorrow.

kevin: follow-ups: (1) add hopper samples to autotune sweep (seed 50 samples), (2) run microprobe to validate alignment vs memcpy rates, (3) update selector to expose debug traces when it rejects a high-scoring kernel.

anika: tagging @sara to collect profiling notes into the incident doc. I'll file a brief internal postmortem if the regression persists after fixes. thanks team.

sara: Copy — I'll paste nvprof traces + heap maps into the incident doc. also adding a small repro that reproduces the memcpy spike (will post link).

mike: Thanks — will put up PR and link to canary results when available.

kevin: :rocket:
